metadata.title: An Ontology-Based Interoperability Framework for Educational Data Integration
metadata.description:
OBIF-EDI: Synthetic Dataset, Ontology and Measurement Notebook for Educational Data Interoperability Evaluation

This record provides the synthetic dataset, OWL ontology, and measurement notebook accompanying the paper "OBIF-EDI: An Ontology-Based Interoperability Framework for Educational Data Integration."

Dataset. The dataset contains 9,165 first-year student records from 13 establishments of Mohammed V University, constructed from official enrollment figures published by the Ministère de l'Enseignement Supérieur, de la Recherche Scientifique et de l'Innovation (MESRSI) for Academic Year 2024-2025 (10% proportional sample, seed=42). It covers six CSV files — LMS learners, SIS students, courses, MOOC runs, xAPI/IMS Caliper activities (64,646 records), and IoT attendance sessions (32,139 records) — implementing six semantic alignment bridges (AR-01 to AR-06) across seven educational system types.

Ontology. The OWL 2 DL ontology (27 classes, 213 triples) formalises the educational domain and encodes six SWRL alignment rules derived from a systematic literature review of 142 empirical studies. Consistency verified with HermiT 1.4.3 under Protégé 5.5.

Notebook. A Google Colab notebook implements the full OBIF-EDI evaluation pipeline: Knowledge Graph construction, REST API measurement (100 real HTTP iterations per scenario), and automated figure and table export. Results are reported as means over 6 independent sessions: SC=94.47%, IS=0.9779, RT=14.72 ± 2.13 ms, SI=0.977 ± 0.21.

Contents. Synthetic dataset (6 CSV files), OWL 2 DL ontology, and measurement notebook.

License. CC BY 4.0.

Citation. Please cite the associated article when using this dataset, ontology, or notebook.

metadata.title: Gastric cancer and ulcerative colitis in East Asians: a genetic association study - analysis code and derived results
metadata.description:
Analysis code, derived variant-level inputs, and result tables for the manuscript
"Gastric cancer and ulcerative colitis in East Asians: a genetic association study"
(Kim JE, Lee H, Oh YE, Kim TS, Min YW, Min BH, Lee JH, Rhee PL).

This archive allows every number reported in the manuscript and in Online Resource 1
to be checked, and allows the analyses to be re-executed from publicly available
genome-wide association study summary statistics. Full genome-wide summary statistics
are not redistributed, because the source databases license them directly to users.

Contents: analysis scripts in R and Python and one Colab notebook; derived variant-level
inputs; all output tables and execution logs; main figures 1-4 and supplementary figure
S2 at 600 dpi and as vector PDF; and a table mapping each analytical output to the
corresponding result in the article and in Online Resource 1.

The study screened 12 East Asian immune-phenotype datasets against gastric cancer,
partitioned the ulcerative colitis instrument into variants inside and outside the
extended major histocompatibility complex, tested regional overlap at HLA-DQA1/DQB1,
and examined associations with other diseases. Analyses used summary statistics from
IEU OpenGWAS and the GWAS Catalog. No individual-level data were used.

See README.md in the archive for data sources, reproduction steps, the output-to-manuscript
mapping, random seeds, and known limitations.

metadata.title: A senescent-cell transcriptional program in intervertebral disc degeneration replicates across cohorts and platforms, whereas the degeneration-grade contrast does not
metadata.description: Cellular senescence is implicated in intervertebral disc (IVD) degeneration, and single-cell reversal-signature analysis is increasingly used to nominate repurposing candidates — usually on the untested assumption that a signature derived from one cohort generalizes. This computational study tests that assumption directly in two independent human nucleus-pulposus single-cell RNA-seq datasets generated on different platforms (GSE244889, 10x Genomics; GSE165722, BD Rhapsody). After isolating the disc-cell population and restricting to clean protein-coding genes, two differential-expression contrasts were compared and their cross-cohort agreement quantified by the Spearman rank-correlation of per-gene log-fold-changes over the shared gene universe. A degeneration-grade contrast (severe vs mild) did not replicate (ρ = +0.015; p = 0.25; 5,937 shared genes) and in fact reversed direction on the collagen/matrix axis, consistent with the non-monotonic nature of disc degeneration. A within-cell senescent-state contrast (senescence-high vs -low nucleus-pulposus cells) did replicate (ρ = +0.287; p = 1.9×10⁻¹²³; 6,508 shared genes), yielding a consensus program of canonical senescence and SASP genes (CDKN1A, TP53, GLB1, SERPINE1, IGFBP3/7, CCL2, CXCL2, MMP3, ADAMTS5) up and chondrogenic nucleus-pulposus identity genes (ACAN, COL2A1, VCAN, FRZB) down. Querying the consensus signature against LINCS L1000 returned a reversal shortlist dominated by NF-κB/IKK inhibitors and HSP90 inhibitors. The contribution is methodological — a within-cell state contrast is a more portable basis for cross-cohort single-cell signature analysis than a disease-stage contrast, and replication should be assessed by rank-correlation over shared genes rather than top-N gene-set overlap. This is not a therapeutic-novelty claim: senotherapeutic approaches to disc degeneration are already well established in the literature, and the work is released openly with no patent claim. All code (Colab notebooks), the consensus signature, and the candidate tables are provided for reproduction.

metadata.title: Supplementary data for Blending physics-based and inverse folding models to disentangle variant effects on stability and function
metadata.description:
Processed data tables for reproducing the figures in Blending physics-based and inverse folding models to disentangle variant effects on stability and function (Galpern et al.). Companion code: https://github.com/DiasFrazerGroup/blend_and_disentangle

Download the zip file(s) below matching the figures you need and extract into the repository's data/ directory (folder names must match: megascale/, human_subset/, mcsa/, cancer/, human_gof_lof/). All files are gzip-compressed CSVs (.csv.gz), readable directly with pandas.read_csv(). All energies are in kcal/mol.

Contents

  • megascale.zip — Fig1, Fig2A–B. Per-model ΔΔG predictions and site-level scores for the megascale benchmark (335 proteins), plus the per-protein AWSEM/model_2 blend calibration weights.

  • human_subset.zip — reference background distribution (200 genes, ~2.1M variants) used for evolutionary-energy percentile thresholds in Fig3/Fig4, and as a gene-browser source.

  • mcsa.zip — Fig2C–E. Per-site pure and AWSEM-blend model scores at M-CSA enzyme active sites (880 enzymes), plus per-protein-mean AUPRC for active-site prediction.

  • cancer.zip — Fig3. Predicted and observed variant scores across 80 cancer genes (oncogenes, tumor suppressors, kinases, GTPases).

  • human_gof_lof.zip — Fig4. Predicted variant scores across 714 genes, plus a curated HGMD/gnomAD variant set annotated by gain-of-function/loss-of-function mechanism.

To reproduce the figures, clone the GitHub repository above and run the notebooks in notebooks/ (compatible with local Jupyter, Google Colab, and Kaggle — Colab/Kaggle download this data automatically).

Terminology

  • de_fold = Folding Energy Change (ΔΔG prediction) [kcal/mol]
  • psi_evo = Evolutionary Score (ESM1v masked logits, inverted sign) [a. u.]
  • kbTsel × psi_evo = Evolutionary Energy Change (protein-specific rescaling of the ESM1v masked logits) [kcal/mol]
  • de_dark = Dark Energy Change [kcal/mol] = kbTsel × psi_evo − de_fold 

Unqualified de_fold/de_dark refer to the primary AWSEM-PottsMPNN blend used throughout the paper. Where a table also carries other models side by side, that same blend is spelled out as de_fold_blend_awsem_pottsmpnn / de_dark_blend_awsem_pottsmpnn.

metadata.title: Розвиток цифрової компетентності майбутніх фахівців авіаційної галузі засобами технологій штучного інтелекту
metadata.description:
У статті обґрунтовується необхідність та доцільність розвитку цифрової компетентності майбутніх фахівців авіаційної галузі засобами технологій штучного інтелекту (ШІ).

Авторкою висвітлено методичні аспекти вибіркового освітнього компонента «Штучний інтелект в авіаційних системах», розробленого та апробованого в Українській державній льотній академії.

Методика базується на двокомпонентному підході до організації освітньої діяльності:

  • Практико-орієнтований компонент: спрямований на формування навичок ефективної взаємодії з сучасними ШІ-інструментами (великими мовними моделями, генеративними сервісами) через промпт-інжиніринг для вирішення професійних завдань без потреби у програмуванні.
  • Концептуально-дослідницький компонент: забезпечує глибоке розуміння базових принципів машинного навчання, комп'ютерного зору та обробки природної мови. У межах цього компонента здобувачі здійснюють практичне навчання моделей (зокрема, перцептрона для розпізнавання рукописних цифр з датасету MNIST), а також працюють з алгоритмами детектування об'єктів у середовищі Google Colab.

Наскрізною дидактичною лінією є професійна спрямованість: вивчаються приклади застосування машинного навчання для аналізу польотних даних, навігації БПЛА, моніторингу інфраструктури та аналізу звітів про безпеку. 

Доведено, що поєднання цих підходів розвиває здатність критично оцінювати згенеровану інформацію, розуміти обмеження алгоритмів та формує відповідальне ставлення до етичних аспектів використання ШІ, що є фундаментальним для забезпечення безпеки польотів.

metadata.title: Hybrid Bias Correction of IMERG Late Run V07 over Indonesia (2001-2025): Input Data, Land-Sea Masks, and Corrected Products
metadata.description:
This deposit contains the full input, mask, and output data bundle for the hybrid statistical-deep learning bias correction of daily IMERG Late Run V07 precipitation over Indonesia (95-141 deg E, -11 to 6 deg N) for the period 2001-2025. The bundle accompanies the companion paper, Istanto, B., Boer, R., Santikayasa, I. P. (2026), A Modular and Transferable Framework for Enhancing Satellite-Derived Daily Precipitation: Adjusting Values, Aligning Distributions, and Preserving Extremes, Remote Sensing 18(14), 2298, https://doi.org/10.3390/rs18142298, and the open-source code at https://github.com/bennyistanto/hybrid-bias-correction.

The framework combines three correction stages applied per 10-day window (dekad). Linear Scaling matches the long-term mean. Empirical Quantile Mapping with a Generalized Pareto Distribution tail (80th-percentile threshold) reshapes the full daily distribution. A lightweight two-layer convolutional network refines the spatial residual on extreme days. A station-density confidence mask, built from the BMKG gauge network, modulates the CNN influence so that the correction degrades gracefully to LSEQM in gauge-sparse areas.

input.zip contains

1. IMERG Late Run V07 (idn_imergl.nc4, 2001-01-01 to 2025-12-31)
2. IMERG Final Run V07 baseline (idn_imergf.nc4, 2001-01-01 to 2025-09-30)
3. CPC-UNI regridded to 0.1 deg (idn_cpcuni.nc4) and at its native 0.5 deg resolution (idn_cpcuni_native05.nc4)
4. BMKG station location and daily observation CSVs.

mask.zip contains the Indonesia land-sea mask at 0.1 deg together with the area-of-interest subsets used for clipping (idn_subset.nc).

output.zip contains

1. Per-method corrected products (corrected_ls, corrected_lseqm, corrected_lseqmdl)
2. Per-method performance metrics (metrics_ls, metrics_lseqm, metrics_lseqmdl)
3. Continuous Quality Index outputs (quality_ls, quality_lseqm, quality_lseqmdl)
4. Station-density confidence mask
5. Independent BMKG station validation CSVs
6. Figures

trained_models.zip contains the trained CNN models, one per dekad.

window_diagnostics.zip contains the derived arrays behind the temporal-alignment analysis, together with the per-station half-hourly cache they are built from (2001 to 2021, one file per year, matching the span of the BMKG station record). These are computed from the raw half-hourly IMERG-L archive rather than from the daily inputs in this deposit, so the other bundles cannot reproduce them. The gridded arrays are split at the satellite transition: 2001 to 2013 for the TRMM-input era and 2015 onward for the GPM era, with 2014 excluded as a transition year. Two GPM windows are included, one ending in 2021 so that it is comparable with the station-based analysis, and one running to the end of the satellite record. The full-record array was assembled by pooling the shorter window with a later increment that was not retained; because these are additive sufficient statistics, that increment is recovered by subtraction from the two files included here, and the README gives the four lines needed. The README also maps each array to the scripts that write and read it. Those scripts are in the thesis repository at https://github.com/bennyistanto/msc-thesis under scripts/; this bundle contains data only.

All gridded files are float32 NetCDF with zlib compression on a common 0.1 degree lat-lon grid, with precipitation in mm/day following the IMERG-L source. The metrics, quality-assessment, and station-density files declare Conventions: CF-1.8; the corrected-precipitation files in this bundle do not, because that attribute was added to the corrected-product writer in framework release v2026.07, after these data were produced. The CPC-UNI 0.5 degree file is kept on the original gauge-analysis grid and is used by the parameter-fitting path that avoids the 5x5 nearest-neighbour block boundary. The run used blend_alpha = 0.70, gpd_threshold_percentile = 80, and station-density saturation_count = 2. These three parameters were not formally optimised and were chosen by inspection. Users adapting the framework to another region should treat them as sensitivity parameters rather than fixed defaults. Outputs written by v2026.07 and later additionally record these parameters, the framework version, and the source commit as global attributes; files in this deposit predate that change.

To reproduce the outputs from the inputs, clone the code repository, point config.yml at the directories in this bundle, and run notebooks 02 through 06 in sequence. A smaller Bali example (about 11 MB) ships with the code repository so users can validate the toolchain on a free Google Colab session before downloading the full Indonesia bundle. Full documentation is available at https://bennyistanto.github.io/hybrid-bias-correction. If you use these data, please cite both this Zenodo deposit and the companion paper (https://doi.org/10.3390/rs18142298).

NASA GPM IMERG V07 data are courtesy of the NASA Goddard Earth Sciences Data and Information Services Center. CPC Unified gauge-based daily precipitation data are provided by the NOAA Physical Sciences Laboratory. BMKG station observations are provided by the Indonesian Agency for Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics.

metadata.title: Analysis code supporting "Solar and Wind Expansion and Uneven Fossil-Generation Displacement Across 29 Emerging and Developing Economies"
metadata.description:
This repository contains the reproducible analysis code for the study “Solar and Wind Expansion and Uneven Fossil-Generation Displacement Across 29 Emerging and Developing Economies.” The software is provided as a Google Colab notebook and a Python script and reproduces the complete analytical workflow for 29 countries over 2010–2024.

The code:

  • imports and harmonizes Ember Yearly Electricity Data, World Bank World Development Indicators, and optional Our World in Data energy series;

  • constructs the balanced country-year and annual-change panels;

  • calculates the gross fossil-displacement ratio, clean-growth coverage, electricity-balance residuals, and annual transition categories;

  • estimates two-way fixed-effects models with country-clustered, Driscoll–Kraay, and restricted wild-cluster-bootstrap inference;

  • performs influence, multicollinearity, normalization, and leave-one-country-out robustness checks;

  • evaluates prospective structural, ex-post diagnostic, and full-balance logistic classifiers using leave-one-country-out validation;

  • produces discrimination, calibration, Brier-score, precision-recall, and country-bootstrap uncertainty estimates;

  • exports the processed datasets, out-of-fold predictions, fold-specific coefficients, manuscript tables, supplementary tables, figure source data, and publication figures.

The default configuration uses Python 3.12, a fixed random seed of 42, 999 wild-cluster-bootstrap replications, and 2,000 country-cluster bootstrap replications for the principal classification analyses. Required package specifications are supplied in requirements.txt and environment.yml, and execution instructions are provided in README.md.

The repository does not redistribute the original public source datasets. Users must obtain the required Ember and World Bank files, and the optional Our World in Data files, from their original providers and upload them using the filenames documented in the README.
